question: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and healthcare-associated infections remain major public health threats in Europe, causing over 35 000 deaths annually and affecting 4.3 million patients each year in EU and European Economic Area healthcare settings.

Medical technologies, including diagnostics, infection prevention, surveillance and stewardship tools, are essential to preventing infections, improving antimicrobial use and supporting progress under the 2023 Council recommendation on AMR1. However, uptake remains uneven across Member States. In the light of the above: 1.

How will the Commission monitor and support Member States’ implementation of the Council recommendation, including the uptake of diagnostics (including in primary care settings), infection prevention and surveillance tools, while linking this to the EU targets for 2030?

Will the Commission conduct an interim EU-level assessment before the four-year review, covering Member State progress, implementation gaps and best practice, to inform future reporting and policy development?

Does the Commission plan to provide any additional financial, technical or policy support for national action plans on AMR and wider uptake of infection prevention, diagnostics (including point-of-care testing), surveillance and stewardship technologies?
Council recommendation of 13 June 2023 on stepping up EU actions to combat antimicrobial resistance in a One Health approach (OJ C 220, 22.6.2023, p. 1). 1
